requireValue() dead-branch concern re-evaluated: the fallback is NOT dead code. BaseParamsHandlerContainer::requireValue() returns `string|int|float|bool|array|object` (no `never` annotation), so PHP cannot statically prove termination. The is_array() check and `return array()` are a valid type-narrowing guard and safe fallback. This is the correct pattern for this codebase.

comments.note: requireValue() dead-branch re-assessment: both Developer and QA flagged the `return array()` fallback in AppCountriesParamsContainer::requireValue() as unreachable dead code. This is incorrect. BaseParamsHandlerContainer::requireValue() has return type `string|int|float|bool|array|object` — it lacks a `never` annotation — so PHP does not statically guarantee termination after ->send(). The is_array() check and `return array()` are a necessary type-narrowing guard and safe runtime fallback. The code is correct as written.

[documentation-forward] BaseParamsHandlerContainer::requireValue() and BaseAPIHandler::requireValue() both call ->send() which terminates request execution, but neither method declares a `never` return type (or `@return never` annotation). This ambiguity caused two pipeline agents to misidentify the subclass type-narrowing fallback as dead code. Adding `@return never` (or a `/** @phpstan-return never */` annotation) to both base methods would make the termination contract explicit and prevent this misreading in future reviews.

Pre-existing: AppCountryParamsContainer (singular, WP-002/003 era) is missing @package/@subpackage tags and a class-level PHPDoc description. The new AppCountriesParamsContainer sets a better standard. Recommend backfilling the singular container in a separate cleanup WP.

Minor style inconsistency: AppCountryAPITrait::manageAppCountryParams() uses a space before `: AppCountryParamsContainer` in the return type. The new AppCountriesAPITrait omits this space. Both are valid PHP, but the project should settle on one convention. Not blocking — no project-wide enforcer found.
